key_insight: A data-driven impeller wall model calibrated from PIV and torque data enables efficient LES of von Kármán flow while preserving long-time metastable state-switching dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to study high-Re turbulent rotating flows without the prohibitive cost of blade-resolved simulations, supporting longer and larger LES campaigns.
method: Parametrize impeller-region velocity with B-splines and couple it to LES through momentum forcing.
Infer an initial coefficient set with ODIL using RANS constraints, PIV measurements, and torque data.
Refine coefficients with CMA-ES to match LES time-averaged velocity and torque to experiments.
evidence_signal: The model is evaluated against experimental PIV and torque measurements and, in long-duration LES, reproduces the mean bulk flow and metastable switching behavior.
watch_item: The approach depends on quality experimental coverage and careful calibration; mismatches in the optically inaccessible region or torque data can limit transferability.
paper_title: Optimal, Data-Driven Wall Models for Efficient Large Eddy Simulations of Metastable von Kármán Flows
